record.original_question: Consider the generalized Smarandache palindrome numbers formed by concatenations of positive integer blocks in the symmetric patterns a_1 a_2 ... a_n a_n ... a_2 a_1 or a_1 a_2 ... a_{n-1} a_n a_{n-1} ... a_2 a_1. Are there infinitely many prime numbers among these generalized Smarandache palindromes?

evidence.quote: Conjecture: There are infinitely many primes which are GSP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A generalized Smarandache palindrome (GSP) is a positive integer whose decimal representation can be partitioned into a concatenation of nonempty blocks of digits B_1 B_2 ... B_k (each B_i being the decimal representation of a positive integer, with no requirement that B_i have no leading zeros internally beyond the usual representation of positive integers) such that one of the following symmetry patterns holds:

- (even case) k = 2n and the block sequence has the form B_1, B_2, ..., B_n, B_n, ..., B_2, B_1;
- (odd case) k = 2n-1 and the block sequence has the form B_1, B_2, ..., B_{n-1}, B_n, B_{n-1}, ..., B_2, B_1.

In other words, the ordered list of blocks reads the same forwards and backwards. (Ordinary digit-palindromes are the special case where each block has length 1.)

Question: Do there exist infinitely many prime numbers that are generalized Smarandache palindromes?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether there are infinitely many primes among generalized Smarandache palindromes is stated as a conjecture in the Smarandache problem literature. No proof or disproof is reported in available sources; even the analogous classical question of whether there are infinitely many ordinary palindromic primes is widely regarded as open. Hence this generalized version is considered open.

status_evidence.title: Palindrome Studies (Part 1)
status_evidence.snippet: Study of Smarandache generalized palindromes applied to prime numbers; concept of extended palindromes introduced.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of generalized Smarandache palindrome and the search for primes among them is treated as an ongoing investigation, not a settled theorem.

status_evidence.title: Conjectures on Primes (I)
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of conjectures on primes in the Smarandache framework, including palindromic-type primes.
status_evidence.claim: Infinitude of primes of these palindromic forms is listed as a conjecture rather than a theorem.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic prime - Simple English Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether there are infinitely many palindromic primes in base 10.
status_evidence.claim: Even the classical infinitude-of-palindromic-primes question is open, supporting that the generalized version is open.
